key_insight: LeapAlign enables reward-based post-training of flow matching models to influence any generation step by building short two-step trajectories, letting gradients reach early timesteps without the memory/instability of backpropagating full long trajectories.
problem_solved: Directly backpropagating reward gradients through long flow-matching generation trajectories is memory-intensive and prone to gradient explosion, preventing effective updates to early generation steps that determine global image structure.
method: Construct two-step (local) trajectories that 'leap' across multiple original timesteps so each update only backpropagates through a short segment.
Use these two-step trajectories to propagate reward gradients to arbitrary generation steps, enabling post-training fine-tuning while avoiding full long-horizon backprop.
Integrate the approach into existing flow-matching pipelines so models can be aligned to human preferences with controlled memory and stabilized gradients.
impact: Makes alignment-fine-tuning of flow-matching image generators practical and scalable, improving global structure control and preference alignment without prohibitive compute or unstable training.
visual_elements: Diagram comparing long-horizon backprop (many steps, high memory, exploding gradient) vs two-step leap trajectories (short segments, low memory, stable gradients).
Schematic showing a generation timeline with arrows indicating how reward gradients jump back to early timesteps using two-step trajectories.
Before/after examples illustrating improved global image structure or preference-aligned outputs after LeapAlign fine-tuning.
Chart of memory usage and gradient norm vs number of backpropagated steps (showing LeapAlign constant/low memory and bounded gradients).
paper_title: LeapAlign: Post-Training Flow Matching Models at Any Generation Step by Building Two-Step Trajectories
paper_authors: Zhanhao Liang, Tao Yang, Jie Wu, Chengjian Feng, Liang Zheng
